body_markdown:
The folks at Mercedes-AMG have been quite busy, it seems. Meet the new Mercedes‑AMG CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung ( *gesundheit!* ), a limited-run, track-melting weapon.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Mercedes-Benz AG


This menacing mouthful (“Spezialanfertigung” is German for “custom-made item”) is the latest product in a fairly new classification of Mercedes vehicles dubbed the[Mythos Series](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-future-of-amg-mythos-maybachs-and-evs/) . The AMG experts in Affalterbach will hand-craft each CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung to ensure top-notch fit and finish. It’s the second Mythos Series vehicle we’ve seen; the first was the[Mercedes-AMG PureSpeed](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/mercedes-amg-purespeed-channels-f1-for-first-mythos-masterpiece/) , an open-top, F1-style Halo-protected two-seater revealed in 2024. A mere 250 examples were produced. The Spezialanfertigung will be even rarer; just 30 are slated for production.


Mercedes-Benz AG


The engineers at AMG began with a simple question: How can a CLE be developed even further toward maximum driving dynamics? It’s an interesting starting point, because the current[CLE 53 Coupe](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2024-mercedes-amg-cle-53-coupe-gets-boosted-by-electric-and-exhaust-gas-turbos/) features a hybridized, turbocharged inline-six under the hood. The CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung, by contrast, will use a tuned version of the vaunted 4.0-liter twin-turbo M177 V-8. Relative to the sixer’s 443 hp, the eight-pot used here produces a whopping 637 hp.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Other notable changes made in service of engaging dynamics: This special-edition model does without the 4Matic+ all-wheel-drive system common on many other AMG products; all that juice goes exclusively to the rear wheels. The change saves weight and will certainly alter the car’s character—particularly out of corners. The electronically controlled limited-slip rear differential can shuffle torque side to side or, in the right conditions, support controlled drifting, AMG says.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Mercedes-Benz AG


With a nine-speed automatic transmission and an adapted launch control system, the CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung can scamper from zero to 62 mph in just 3.9 seconds on its way to a top speed of 193 mph. That’s hustling for a car that still weighs 4178 lbs (which, by the way, is roughly 375 lbs lighter than the CLE 53 Coupe this brute is based on).


Mercedes-Benz AG


Mercedes-Benz AG


A specially developed coliover system, co-developed by Mercedes-AMG and KW Automotive, handles the suspension duties. A four-way adjustable damper system adorns all four corners, and the trick shocks boast independently configurable high- and low-speed settings for both rebound and compression.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Between the muscle and the suspension, this thing will build pace quickly, but thanks to a high-performance composite brake system, you should be able to keep things in check just fine. Large air intakes in the front bumper cool massive 16.5-inch front rotors paired with six-piston fixed calipers. Out back, 14.2-inch composite rotors and a single-piston floating caliper pitch in extra clamping effort.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Mercedes-Benz AG


Mercedes-Benz AG


About that body: We’re getting whiffs of a German[Mustang GTD](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-mustang-gtd-first-drive-true-to-its-roots/) here, or maybe a German iteration of the[2020 Shelby GT500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/secrets-of-the-2020-shelby-gt500-revealed/) . Those vents behind the front wheels (and the wheels themselves) scream GTD, while the fangs up front on the grille lean GT500. Relative to the CLE 53 Coupe, this CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung is 2.4 inches wider to help add stability, swallow larger wheels and tires, and up the overall menacing look. Those wider front fenders are made from carbon fiber, of course, as are the side sills, front fascia, hood, roof, and the rear apron and diffuser.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Aerodynamics were obviously important on this CLE. The front splitter can be manually adjusted between two positions, “street” and “race.” Ditto for the center section of the rear wing. At top speed, AMG says the CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung produces more than 550 lbs of squish.


Mercedes-Benz AG


Pricing details are nonexistent, not that it matters all that much—all 30 examples were spoken for even before this thing’s world debut. Here’s to hoping at least a few examples see real use on good roads and great tracks, because we’d bet this thing can absolutely get down.
